questions.q: How long should your quotations be in the writer's effect answer?
questions.why: Short quotations show exactly which words you are analysing.

questions.q: "Rain hammered on the tin roof." Which comment would earn most credit?
options: It creates a vivid image and makes the reader want to read on
"Hammered" suggests heavy, violent blows, so the rain seems loud and relentless
questions.why: Top answers unpack the connotations of a specific word, not just name a device or give meaning.

questions.q: How many choices does the writer's effect question ask for?
options: Two from each of three paragraphs
Three from each of two named paragraphs
One from each paragraph in the text
questions.why: Choose three from each named paragraph, including imagery.

questions.q: "Fog crept along the river." Explain the meaning and the effect of "crept".
questions.model: Meaning: the fog moved slowly and quietly along the river. Effect: "crept" personifies the fog as someone sneaking up unseen, making it seem secretive and threatening and creating a sense of unease.
points: effect: connotations of sneaking / sinister, creating unease
